track.title: Data and Tokens
track.summary: Start from bytes, Unicode, characters, and tokenization before any model training happens.

checkpoint.question: Why can the same visible character use different byte sequences?
checkpoint.answer: Because text is encoded into bytes using a character encoding such as UTF-8, and visible characters can map to one or more code points and byte sequences.

checkpoint.question: What does a character tokenizer lose compared with a learned subword tokenizer?
checkpoint.answer: It creates long sequences and does not learn frequent reusable chunks such as common words, prefixes, or suffixes.

checkpoint.question: What does one BPE merge do?
checkpoint.answer: It finds a frequent adjacent token pair and replaces that pair with a new token, shortening sequences while expanding the vocabulary.
